section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the present (single) study, which analyzed data from the YouBeauty.com Body Image Survey (YBIS) with respondents from the West (primarily the United States). The study measured two aspects of body image — weight-related body dissatisfaction and body appreciation — and examined how age and education influence BMI, which in turn affect body dissatisfaction and appreciation, with those two body-image variables predicted to have opposite effects on subjective happiness.
section_summary.evidence_source: In the present study, we examined associations between women's body image and subjective happiness using data from the YouBeauty.com Body Image Survey (YBIS). More specifically, respondents from the West (primarily the United States) completed two measures of body image, namely weight-related body dissatisfaction (actual-ideal weight discrepancy) and body appreciation. We further examined the impact of respondent age and education on the associations between body image and subjective happiness. We proposed a hypothesised model, derived from the above review of the extant literature, in which education and age shape respondent BMI, which in turn affect body dissatisfaction and body appreciation. The latter two variables were predicted to affect subjective happiness in opposite directions (see Fig. 1).

section_summary.extract_value: This section describes a single study using data from the YouBeauty.com Body Image Survey (YBIS) with respondents from the West (primarily the United States) to examine links between women's body image and subjective happiness. The study measured weight-related body dissatisfaction (actual-ideal weight discrepancy) and body appreciation, and tested a model where education and age shape BMI, which in turn affects body dissatisfaction and body appreciation; those two variables were predicted to affect subjective happiness in opposite directions. The hypothesised model is illustrated in Fig. 1, which reports standardized path coefficients for the US sample.
